title: If the Service Layer Does All the Real Work, What Is the LLM Actually For?

data.text:
A lot of AI architecture diagrams look almost disappointing once you make them production-safe.

The LLM does not own the database. It does not decide permissions. It should not enforce business rules. It should not directly execute payments, update records, or determine whether a user is authorized.

So an obvious question appears:

If the service layer is doing all the important work, why do we need the LLM at all?

That question is actually the key to understanding production AI architecture.
